summary: The APAC expansion carries medium-high risk due to unvalidated compliance requirements in Japan, a revenue model dependent on an enterprise segment the team cannot access without ISMAP certification, and a payments timeline with no margin for slippage. Singapore is lower risk but the standalone unit economics have not been validated. Recommend proceeding with guards: greenlight Singapore planning but gate Japan commitment on legal review and certification timeline.
thesis_under_test: The company can launch in Japan and Singapore by Q4 using the existing SaaS platform with localization and a distribution partner in Japan.

key_assumptions.assumption: The payments team can deliver a lightweight multi-currency layer (USD, JPY, SGD) in three months
key_assumptions.evidence_from_transcript: They think they can do a lightweight multi-currency layer in three months if we limit to USD, JPY, and SGD only.

key_assumptions.assumption: The revenue model works with 30% enterprise mix by month six in Japan
key_assumptions.evidence_from_transcript: The revenue model assumes 30% enterprise mix by month six. If we're SMB-only, we'd need to roughly double the customer count to hit the same revenue target.

key_assumptions.assumption: Singapore can be served from existing US-East and EU-West infrastructure with acceptable latency
key_assumptions.evidence_from_transcript: Singapore is easier — we can serve from our existing infrastructure with acceptable latency.

failure_modes.title: Japanese invoicing non-compliance blocks enterprise sales
failure_modes.why_it_fails: Japan's Qualified Invoice System imposes strict requirements on invoicing. The legal team has not reviewed these requirements. If invoices are non-compliant, enterprise buyers cannot claim tax credits, making the product commercially unviable for the target enterprise segment. The team has no legal review underway and the Q4 timeline leaves no room to remediate.
leading_indicators: Legal review has not started by end of month
Legal review reveals requirements that conflict with current billing system architecture
First Japanese enterprise prospect raises invoicing compliance during sales process
failure_modes.mitigation: Start legal review of Qualified Invoice System requirements this week. Make Japan launch gate on legal sign-off. Do not commit to Japan timeline until invoicing compliance is confirmed feasible within the billing system.

failure_modes.title: ISMAP certification timeline makes Japan enterprise market inaccessible until mid next year
failure_modes.why_it_fails: ISMAP certification requires 4-6 months. Without it, the company can only sell to SMB customers in Japan. The revenue model assumes 30% enterprise mix — without enterprise, customer count must roughly double to hit targets. SMB-only Japan is a fundamentally different business case than what was proposed.
leading_indicators: ISMAP certification process not initiated within 30 days
Compliance team estimates timeline longer than 6 months
Revised SMB-only revenue projections show negative unit economics
failure_modes.mitigation: Decouple Japan timeline from Singapore. Begin ISMAP certification process immediately as a background workstream. Remodel Japan revenue projections for SMB-only scenario and present to leadership as the realistic base case.

failure_modes.title: Lightweight multi-currency payments layer slips past July, forcing USD-only Japan launch
failure_modes.why_it_fails: The three-month estimate for the payments layer is based on 'preliminary conversations' — not a committed engineering plan. If the payments team has competing priorities or the scope grows, the July target slips. A USD-only launch in Japan triggers the compliance issues with manual currency conversion that Sophie flagged.
leading_indicators: Payments team has not committed engineering resources by end of next sprint
Scope of multi-currency layer expands beyond USD/JPY/SGD
Payments team reports competing priorities that delay start date
failure_modes.mitigation: Get a firm commitment from the payments team lead this week: staffing, start date, and milestones. If they cannot commit, plan for USD-only billing and assess whether Japan launch is viable under that constraint.

failure_modes.title: Singapore standalone unit economics do not justify expansion without Japan enterprise revenue
failure_modes.why_it_fails: The original proposal bundled Japan and Singapore. If Japan is delayed to Q2+ next year and Singapore goes alone, the combined revenue projection no longer applies. Singapore-only unit economics have not been modeled. If they don't stand up, leadership may reject the expansion entirely, including the Series C narrative benefit.
leading_indicators: Revised Singapore-only projections show payback period beyond 18 months
Board feedback indicates APAC presence requires Japan, not just Singapore
Customer pipeline in Singapore is thinner than projected
failure_modes.mitigation: Kenji's revised plan (due next Friday) must include Singapore standalone P&L with realistic customer acquisition timeline. If the numbers don't work, present leadership with a phased plan that shows Singapore as a beachhead with Japan as the revenue driver.

adversarial_questions: If the payments team's three-month estimate is based on 'preliminary conversations,' what happens when it becomes a committed project with real scope review — does the timeline survive?

The revenue model assumes 30% enterprise in Japan by month six, but enterprise requires ISMAP certification that takes 4-6 months. How was that model built without accounting for certification lead time?
If Singapore standalone doesn't justify the expansion economically, are we spending Q3-Q4 engineering effort on a market that only makes sense as a precursor to Japan — which is 6+ months away?
The Nomura partnership is unsigned and Japan-specific. If Japan slips to Q2 next year, will Nomura still be available and interested, or have we lost that window?
What is the actual incremental engineering cost of this expansion — not just infra, but localization, compliance, support, and payments — and does leadership understand that number?

decision_recommendation.rationale: Singapore is viable with existing infrastructure and no special certifications. However, the Japan component of the proposal has multiple blocking dependencies (ISMAP, legal review, payments) that make Q4 unrealistic. Proceeding with Singapore-first is reasonable if the standalone economics justify it. Japan should be re-evaluated once legal review, ISMAP timeline, and payments commitment are confirmed.
required_next_checks: Kenji delivers revised Singapore-standalone plan with unit economics by next Friday
Diana provides firm APAC region buildout estimate by Wednesday and ISMAP certification timeline by end of next week
Legal review of Japan Qualified Invoice System requirements initiated this week
Payments team provides committed timeline and staffing for lightweight multi-currency layer
